questions.question: An enlarged thyroid, also known as ______, is the most common manifestation of iodine deficiency in adults.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goitre**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **A goitre **is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, which is a butterfly-shaped gland located in the neck.
 
• The most common cause worldwide is **iodine deficiency. **
 
• The thyroid uses iodine, a mineral found in some foods and in iodized salt, to make thyroid hormones.
 
• When your body doesn't get enough iodine, the thyroid works harder to make these hormones, and this extra work can cause the gland to enlarge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Hashimoto's Thyroiditis: **This is an autoimmune condition in which the body's immune system attacks the thyroid, leading to inflammation and interfering with its ability to produce thyroid hormones.

 
 
• Over time, it often leads to hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid). While it can lead to an enlarged thyroid, it's not specifically related to iodine deficiency.
 
 
 
• **Cretinism**: This is a very rare condition caused by severe, untreated congenital hypothyroidism (low thyroid hormone levels at birth).
 
 
• It results in stunted physical and mental growth. While iodine deficiency in a pregnant woman can lead to cretinism in her baby, this condition isn't a manifestation of iodine deficiency in adults.
 
 
 
• **Graves' Disease: **This is an autoimmune condition that causes hyperthyroidism (overactive thyroid), not an enlarged thyroid due to iodine deficiency.
 
 
• In Graves' disease, the immune system creates antibodies that cause the thyroid to grow and make more thyroid hormone than the body needs.

questions.question: A goalkeeper in a football game pulls his hands backwards after holding the ball shot at the goal. This enables the goalkeeper to

options.text: increase the rate of change of momentum
decrease the rate of change of momentum
increase the force exerted by the balls on the hands
exert larger force on the ball

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease the rate of change of momentum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The goalkeeper pulls his hands back to reduce the rate of change of momentum of the ball.
 
• Decreasing the rate of change of momentum also decreases the force exerted on his hands.
 
• By pulling his hands back, the time interval over which the momentum changes is increased.
 
• This action helps in reducing the impact force, making it easier for the goalkeeper to handle the ball.
 
• According to the impulse-momentum theorem, impulse is equal to the change in momentum, and by increasing the time, the force is reduced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impulse**

 
 
• Impulse is the product of force and the time interval during which the force is applied.
 
• It is equal to the change in momentum of the object.
 
 
 
• **Momentum**
 
 
• Momentum is the product of mass and velocity of an object.
 
• It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Force**
 
 
• Force is any interaction that, when unopposed, will change the motion of an object.
 
• It can cause an object with mass to change its velocity (to accelerate).

questions.question: The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 conducted by the government of India ranked households in how many categories?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 was conducted by the government of India to provide comprehensive data on various socio-economic indicators.
 
• The SECC 2011 categorized households into three main categories based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The three categories were: 1) Deprived households, 2) Automatically included households, and 3) Automatically excluded households.
 
• The categorization helped the government identify and target households for various welfare schemes and programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC):**

 
 
• The SECC is a comprehensive survey conducted to collect data on various socio-economic parameters and caste information.
 
• It aims to identify households living below the poverty line and categorize them based on their socio-economic status.
 
• The data from SECC is used to implement and monitor various social welfare schemes and programs.
 
• It provides insights into the living conditions, educational status, employment, and other socio-economic aspects of households.
 
 
 
• **Deprived Households:**
 
 
• These households are identified based on specific deprivation criteria such as lack of housing, education, or employment.
 
• They are considered eligible for various government welfare schemes and programs aimed at improving their socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Included Households:**
 
 
• These households are automatically included in the welfare programs based on certain predefined criteria such as homelessness or being a bonded laborer.
 
• The criteria for automatic inclusion are designed to ensure that the most vulnerable and marginalized sections of society receive immediate assistance.
 
 
 
• **Automatically Excluded Households:**
 
 
• These households are excluded from welfare programs based on specific criteria such as owning a motorized vehicle or having a government job.
 
• The criteria for automatic exclusion are designed to ensure that resources are allocated to those who are truly in need.

• **Shifting agriculture **is another name for it. It involves the __slash and burn technique__.
 
• **Multiple crops **are grown in the same field at the same time to __make the most of the limited land available. __

questions.question: How many members of the Rajya Sabha can be nominated by the President of India?

__
 
• The **President of India** can nominate **12 members** to the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• These nominations are made to represent people with special knowledge or practical experience in fields like **literature, science, art, and social service**.
 
• **Article 80** of the Indian Constitution specifies the nomination process for the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The nominated members enjoy the same rights and privileges as elected members, except the right to vote in the election of the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect

 **Rajya Sabha**
 The **upper house** of India's **bicameral Parliament**, also known as the **Council of States**.
 
 

 **Term**
 Members of the Rajya Sabha serve for a term of **six years**, with one-third of the members retiring every two years.
 
 

 **Total Seats**
 The Rajya Sabha can have a **maximum of 250 members**, including the 12 nominated by the President.
 
 

 **Role**
 The Rajya Sabha acts as a **reviewing chamber** for legislation proposed by the Lok Sabha (the lower house).
 
 

 **Eligibility**
 Members must be **at least 30 years old**, be **citizens of India**, and meet other criteria as specified by law.

questions.question:
Select the correct equation(s) that relate(s) the final and initial velocity of a freely falling object with respect to time.

(A) s = ut +2at²

(B) v = u + (1)/(2)at

(C) (v - u) = at
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Equation (C), (v-u)=at, is derived from the basic definition of acceleration: acceleration (a) is the rate of change of velocity with time (t).
 
• This equation applies directly to uniformly accelerated motion, such as that of a freely falling object under gravity.
 
• It relates the final velocity (v) of an object to its initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and the time of travel (t).
 
• Equations (A) and (B) are not correctly written or applicable in the context of a freely falling object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of Motion:**

 
 
• There are three primary equations of motion that describe the behavior of objects in uniformly accelerated linear motion:
 
 
• v=u+at
 
• s=ut+(1)/(2)at²
 
• v²=u²+2as
 
 
 
• These equations are essential in classical mechanics and are used to predict future motion based on current conditions.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:**
 
 
• Uniform acceleration refers to a constant acceleration, meaning the velocity of the object changes at a constant rate.
 
• In the case of free fall, the acceleration due to gravity (g) is approximately 9.81 m/s² near the Earth's surface.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• Free fall is the motion of an object under the influence of gravitational force only.
 
• During free fall, the only force acting on the object is gravity, leading to a uniform acceleration downwards.
 
 
 
• **Initial and Final Velocity:**
 
 
• Initial velocity (u) is the velocity of the object before it starts accelerating.
 
• Final velocity (v) is the velocity of the object after it has been accelerating for a certain period of time.

questions.question: Who among the following leaders was defeated in the 'Battle of Waterloo' in 1815?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Napoleon Bonaparte**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Napoleon Bonaparte** was a French military leader who rose to prominence during the French Revolution and led several successful campaigns during the Revolutionary Wars.
 
• The **Battle of Waterloo** took place on June 18, 1815, near Waterloo in present-day Belgium.
 
• Napoleon Bonaparte was defeated by a coalition of forces led by the Duke of Wellington (British) and Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher (Prussian).
 
• This defeat marked the end of Napoleon's rule as Emperor of the French and led to his second abdication and exile to Saint Helena.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Waterloo**

 
 
• The Battle of Waterloo was fought on Sunday, 18 June 1815, and was a decisive battle that ended the Napoleonic Wars.
 
• It was fought between Napoleon's French Army and the Seventh Coalition, which included British, Dutch, Belgian, and Prussian forces.
 
• The battle saw heavy casualties on both sides, with estimates of around 25,000 French and 23,000 Coalition soldiers killed or wounded.
 
• The defeat at Waterloo led to the restoration of the Bourbon monarchy in France and marked the end of Napoleon's political and military career.
 
 
 
• **Napoleon Bonaparte**
 
 
• Born on August 15, 1769, in Corsica, Napoleon rose rapidly through the ranks of the French army during the French Revolution.
 
• He became Emperor of the French in 1804 and led France in a series of military conquests across Europe.
 
• Napoleon implemented several reforms in France, including the Napoleonic Code, which influenced legal systems worldwide.
 
• After his defeat at Waterloo, Napoleon was exiled to the island of Saint Helena, where he died on May 5, 1821.
 
 
 
• **Duke of Wellington**
 
 
• Arthur Wellesley, 1st Duke of Wellington, was a British Army officer and statesman who defeated Napoleon at the Battle of Waterloo.
 
• He served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom twice and was known for his military and political career.
 
• Wellington's leadership at Waterloo was crucial in the defeat of Napoleon.
 
• He is often referred to as one of Britain's greatest military heroes.
 
 
 
• **Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher**
 
 
• Blücher was a Prussian field marshal who played a key role in the defeat of Napoleon at Waterloo.
 
• He commanded the Prussian forces that arrived to support Wellington's troops during the battle.
 
• Blücher's timely arrival and coordination with Wellington were vital in turning the tide against Napoleon.
 
• He is celebrated as one of the most successful Prussian military leaders.

• Symptoms include rough, scaly skin rashes, gastrointestinal issues, and neurological disturbances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Niacin deficiency can lead to pellagra, characterized by the Four D's.

• Dermatitis is an inflammation of the skin that results in itchy, red, swollen, and sore skin.
 
• In pellagra, dermatitis typically appears symmetrically on sun-exposed areas.
 
 
 
• **Diarrhea**
 
 
• Diarrhea involves frequent, loose, or watery bowel movements.
 
• It is a common symptom of pellagra affecting the gastrointestinal tract.
 
 
 
• **Dementia**
 
 
• Dementia refers to a decline in cognitive function, affecting memory, thinking, and social abilities.
 
• In pellagra, dementia can progress to severe neurological impairment if untreated.

• They show a remarkable continuity from the Indus to the Tista.
 
• Rivers **descending from the Himalayas deposit their load** along the foothills in the form of alluvial fans.
 
• These **alluvial fans have merged together to build up the bhabar belt.**
 
• The **porosity of bhabar** is the most unique feature.
 
• The porosity is **due to deposition of huge number of pebbles and rock debris across the alluvial fans.**
 
• The **streams disappear once** they reach the bhabar region **because of this porosity.**
 
• Therefore, the **area is marked by dry river courses except in the rainy season.**
 
• The Bhabar belt is **comparatively narrow in the east** and extensive in the western and north-western hilly region.
 
• The area is **not suitable for agriculture **and only big trees with large roots thrive in this belt.

questions.question: Which bacteria is found in roots of leguminous plants as symbionts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rhizobium**__.

__**Concept:**__

__
 
• **Microorganisms **are too small and are not visible to naked eyes.
 
• Microorganisms are found in air, water and in the bodies of plants and animals.
 
• They may be **unicellular **or **multicellular**.
 
• Microorganisms are classified into **four major groups**.
 
 
• **Bacteria**- Bacteria convert gaseous nitrogen into a usable form and release it into the soil.
 
• **Fungi**- Fungi are cosmopolitan and occur in air, water, soil and on animals and plants.
 
• **Protozoa**- protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
 
• **Algae**- Algae are largely aquatic both fresh water and marine organisms.
 
 

**Explanation:**__

__
 
• **Leguminous plants belong to the family Fabaceae.**
 
• These **plants have a symbiotic relationship with the soil bacteria** Rhizobium, which lives in their roots.
 
• **Rhizobium **is a **biofertiliser**. 
 
• Biofertilizers are the microorganisms that enrich the nutrient (nitrogen, phosphorous, etc.) quality of the soil.
 
• **Rhizobium is a** **symbiotic bacterium that lives in the root nodules of leguminous ****plants**__ and **fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic compound** (ammonia) and it also fertilizes the soil.
 
• It causes the formation of special structures known as **nodules **within the cell, which fix atmospheric nitrogen.
 
• It accomplishes this with the help of the nitrogenase enzyme, which converts nitrogen to ammonium, a necessary factor for plant growth.
 
• Rhizobium bacteria form symbiotic associations with plants.
 
• **Plants provide them with food and shelter**, and these bacteria fix nitrogen in the soil.

**Kakatiyas Dynasty**

 
• The** Koh-i-Noor diamond** was probably** found in India in the 13th century and was initially owned by the Kakatiya dynasty.**
 
• The Kakatiya dynasty used to** rule over the region in Warangal. **They considered **Goddess ****Bhadrakali****, as their Kul devatha, and the diamond was fitted on the left eye of the deity.**
 
• 
 **In the 14th century, the diamond was acquired by the Khilji dynasty** of the Delhi Sultanate after a **successful raid on Warangal.**
 
 
•

• 
 The diamond was **placed into the Peacock Throne by Shah Jahan**, the fifth Mughal emperor, and later cut by Hortense Borgia, reducing its weight from 793 carats to 186 carats.
 
 
• 
 **In 1739, Nader Shah, the Shah of Persia, invaded Delhi and plundered the Mughal Empire's treasury,** including the Koh-i-Noor diamond.
 
 
• 
 After Nader Shah's assassination and the collapse of his empire, the diamond **came into the hands of one of his generals, Ahmad Shah Durrani.**
 
 
• 
 In 1813, the diamond was **brought back to India by Shah Shuja Durrani and given to Ranjit Singh **in exchange for help reclaiming the throne of Afghanistan.
 
 
•
